[.claude/commands/pr-appr-review.md#scope]

## Scope

- If `$ARGUMENTS` is a **PR URL** (e.g., `https://github.com/org/repo/pull/42`), review that PR — clone the repo if needed (ask first)
- If `$ARGUMENTS` specifies a PR number, review that PR in the current repo
- If `$ARGUMENTS` specifies a repo (e.g., `bootstrap`), review that repo's open PR for its current branch
- Otherwise, find the open PR for the current branch in the current repo
- **A `pr-manager` Agent, where one exists for the repo** (`.github/agents/pr-manager.agent.md`), reads and applies steps 5–7 of this Workflow directly as a post-fix verification pass against the final diff, the same way it reads and applies `/pr-appr-resolve` — not Agent-to-Agent subagent composition, and not this Workflow invoking an Agent, just an Agent reading a Workflow's documented procedure.

[.claude/commands/pr-appr-review.md#workflow]

## Workflow

1. **Parse the input and determine the repo**

   - **PR URL** (e.g., `https://github.com/org/repo/pull/42`):
     - Extract `owner`, `repo`, and `number` from the URL
     - Check if the repo exists locally (in `../repo` or current directory)
     - If **not local**, ask the user before cloning:

       ```text
       This PR is in org/repo which isn't cloned locally. Clone to ../{repo} and review? (yes/no)
       ```

     - If user approves, clone to `../{repo}`, cd into it, and checkout the PR branch:

       ```bash
       gh repo clone {owner}/{repo} ../{repo}
       cd ../{repo}
       gh pr checkout {number}
       ```

     - If user declines, review the diff remotely via `gh pr diff` without cloning (limited — no local file reads)
   - **PR number** — use current repo
   - **Repo name** (e.g., `bootstrap`) — find the open PR for that repo's current branch
   - **Nothing** — find the open PR for the current branch

2. **Pull latest** — run `git pull` to ensure you're reviewing the latest code

3. **Identify the PR** (if not already resolved from URL)
   - If no PR specified, find the open PR for the current branch:

     ```bash
     gh pr list --head "$(git branch --show-current)" --json number,url --jq '.[0]'
     ```

   - If no open PR exists, fall back to reviewing the branch diff against main (local only — no remote comments)

4. **Read the full diff**

   ```bash
   gh pr diff {number}
   ```

   Also read the PR description and commit history to understand intent:

   ```bash
   gh pr view {number} --json title,body,commits
   ```

5. **Analyze every changed EA artifact and AI construct.** A Command cannot invoke an Agent — no `agents:` field mechanism exists for Commands, per `pr-manager.agent.md`'s Scope Boundaries — so this Command applies both governing Skills directly, in its own workflow:
   - For changed EA artifact files, read `.claude/skills/ea-reviewer/SKILL.md` and apply its actual criteria — Authoring Standard Compliance, Content Quality (type-specific judgment questions), Internal Consistency, Cross-Document Consistency, Lifecycle and Change Impact, and Structural/Governance Checks.
   - For changed AI construct files — Skills, Agents, Workflows/Commands/Prompts, Instructions, and file-pattern Instructions, the same taxonomy `pr-manager.agent.md` step 5 defines from `ADR-TEC-020` — read `.claude/skills/ai-reviewer/SKILL.md` and apply its equivalent criteria the same way.
   - Changed files matching neither taxonomy are left to GitHub Copilot's native PR review, per the same scope boundary `ea-reviewer.agent.md` and `ai-review.agent.md` declare.

6. **Check enterprise standards** — discover applicable standards for the changed files:
   - Detect languages in the diff, scan `eap-ref-architecture/standards/technology/` for matching `STD-*` files
   - Check `eap-ref-architecture/patterns/` for patterns the changes should follow
   - Check project conventions in CLAUDE.md

7. **Rank each finding:**

   | Severity | Meaning |
   | --- | --- |
   | **Critical** | Must fix before merge — will cause failures or security issues |
   | **High** | Strongly recommended — significant risk or quality concern |
   | **Medium** | Should fix — improves correctness or maintainability |
   | **Low** | Optional — minor improvement or suggestion |

8. **Present findings to the user for approval before posting**

   Display the full review locally as a table:

   ```text
   ## Review Summary — PR #{number}

   **Verdict:** REQUEST_CHANGES / COMMENT / APPROVE

   | # | Severity | File:Line | Comment |
   | --- | --- | --- | --- |
   | 1 | Critical | src/auth.py:42 | Missing input validation on user_id |
   | 2 | Medium | config.yml:8 | Hardcoded timeout should use env var |
   ```

   Then ask once:

   ```text
   Post {N} comments as {VERDICT}?
   ```

   - **User approves** — post all comments and submit the review
   - **User declines or edits** — adjust per their feedback, then post (no second approval round)

   **Do not post to the remote until the user confirms.**

9. **Post findings as PR review comments on the remote** (after approval)

   Submit a full review with inline comments on specific lines:

   ```bash
   gh api repos/{owner}/{repo}/pulls/{number}/reviews -f event="COMMENT" \
     -f body="<overall summary>" \
     -f 'comments[][path]=<file>' \
     -f 'comments[][position]=<diff position>' \
     -f 'comments[][body]=<finding>'
   ```

   For each finding, post an inline comment on the specific file and line with:
   - Severity tag: `**[Critical]**`, `**[High]**`, `**[Medium]**`, or `**[Low]**`
   - What's wrong and why it matters
   - Suggested fix (code suggestion block if applicable)

   If no findings above Low severity, post a single review comment approving.

10. **Submit verdict and report results**

    Submit the review verdict:

    | Condition | Verdict |
    | --- | --- |
    | Any Critical or High findings | `REQUEST_CHANGES` |
    | Only Medium or Low findings | `COMMENT` |
    | No findings or only praise | `APPROVE` |

    Then report locally: total findings by severity, files reviewed, verdict submitted, and link to the PR.

[.claude/commands/pr-appr-review.md#comment-format]

## Comment Format

Each inline comment follows this format:

````text
**[Severity]** Brief description

<explanation of what's wrong and the impact>

Suggested fix:
```suggestion
<corrected code>
```
````

For non-code findings (docs, config), skip the suggestion block and describe the fix in text.

[.claude/commands/pr-appr-review.md#what-not-to-review]

## What NOT to Review

- Untouched code surrounding the changes — review what changed, not the whole file
- Style preferences that don't violate project standards
- Generated files (SVGs, lock files) — unless the generation looks wrong
- Pre-existing issues in unchanged code — note them separately if critical, but don't block the PR

[.claude/commands/pr-appr-review.md#examples]

## Examples

```text
/pr-appr-review
```

Finds the PR for the current branch, reviews the diff, posts inline comments, submits verdict.

```text
/pr-appr-review 3
```

Reviews PR #3 in the current repo.

```text
/pr-appr-review bootstrap
```

Reviews the open PR in eap-bootstrap.

$ARGUMENTS
